sermons.title: Saving a Nation

shorts.title: Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?
title_options: Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?
What if we want heaven but not His Word?
Have we rejected God ruling over us?
shorts.summary: Israel rejected God ruling over them—wanting heaven and blessings without obedience. Luke 19:14: we will not have this man to rule over us.

shorts.title: Do we only want to hear smooth things?
title_options: Do we only want to hear smooth things?
Are we paying pastors to flatter us?
What if confidence isn’t the same as being okay?
shorts.summary: Groups hire ministers to flatter them—Isaiah 30:10 speak smooth things. Scripture is for righteousness, but many only want to hear that they’re okay.

shorts.title: What if a nation turns back to God?
title_options: What if a nation turns back to God?
Can God relent over a nation?
Is Bible morality an umbrella of protection?
shorts.summary: God will pluck up a disobedient nation—but if that nation turns from evil, He will relent. Bible morality is an umbrella of protection when God judges.

shorts.title: Can the Word still turn a nation?
title_options: Can the Word still turn a nation?
What if speaking the Word is enough?
Where does saving a nation start?
shorts.summary: It’s the Word that must get out—speak it; it convicts and convinces. The turning of a nation starts with the church.

unused_candidates.working_title: Why were these stories written down? / What if nations fall so we can learn?
unused_candidates.core_truth: Romans 15:4 and 1 Cor 10:11 — OT events occurred as examples for our learning when God deals with nations.
unused_candidates.notes: Strong opener; overlap with sermon thesis already covered by if-a-nation-turns / word-turns-a-nation

unused_candidates.working_title: Is the Bible trying to turn us to good works?
unused_candidates.core_truth: 2 Tim 3:16–17 — all Scripture profitable; focus righteousness; turn from bad works to good works via the Spirit.
unused_candidates.notes: Solid shorter punch; keep for follow-up

unused_candidates.working_title: What happens when every man does what’s right in his own eyes?
unused_candidates.core_truth: Judges 17:5–6 setup — no king in Israel; homemade religion; folded partly into blessings-or-his-rule opening.
Unite on Bible moral issues (not secondary disputes); list of things not to fellowship over.
unused_candidates.notes: Strong but long list + culture tangents

sermons.title: Division Part 1

shorts.title: Is church really boring?
title_options: Is church really boring?
Is it the church’s fault we’re bored?
What if church isn’t boring — we just stopped getting involved?
shorts.summary: Young people say church is boring — he said it too, as a clock-watching teen who didn’t get involved. David was glad to go to the house of the Lord; the church is the people.

shorts.title: Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?
title_options: Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?
What if every church spoke the same thing?
Why is a Big Mac the same everywhere — but church isn’t?
shorts.summary: A Big Mac is identical in Brazil, Korea, China and every state. Paul says “speak the same thing” — the Holy Ghost, salvation and holy living should be preached the same in every church.

shorts.title: Can a divided home still stand?
title_options: Can a divided home still stand?
Why do husband and wife need the same truth?
What happens when a family is divided?
shorts.summary: Jesus: a kingdom or house divided against itself will not stand. Husband and wife must stand together in the same truth and show their children Jesus — or the home won’t stand.

shorts.title: Who was really crucified for you?
title_options: Who was really crucified for you?
Is Christ divided?
Which church group is the right one?
shorts.music: “Touching Moments Two - Higher” — Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
shorts.summary: “I am of Paul… Apollos… Peter… Christ.” Only the Christ group is right. Was Paul crucified for you? No pope, priest, denomination or famous minister saves — it is Christ and the Scriptures.

unused_candidates.working_title: Is it the church's fault I left?
unused_candidates.core_truth: He left church as a teen because he wanted to sin, not because of the church; God told him to get in and make a difference.
unused_candidates.notes: Strong personal testimony; overlaps is-church-boring theme.

unused_candidates.working_title: Do we line up with Scripture — or make it line up with us?
unused_candidates.core_truth: Let God be true and every man a liar; voices blaming the church are wrong; we must line up with the Scriptures (suit story).

unused_candidates.working_title: Can the church change the Scriptures to be liked?
unused_candidates.core_truth: The church cannot change the Scriptures because public policy changes.
unused_candidates.notes: Sensitive topics (abortion, sexual sin); would need very careful soft framing.

unused_candidates.working_title: What do our kids actually need to see?
unused_candidates.core_truth: Kids need to see our moral standards, tongue and curbed anger — not just hear about the Second Coming.

unused_candidates.working_title: Why do we tell the world when we disagree?
unused_candidates.core_truth: Judge righteous judgment backed by Scripture; don't blab church disagreements to the world.

unused_candidates.working_title: Are we following a minister — or Jesus?
unused_candidates.core_truth: Follow and imitate Jesus, not ministers or church groups; Paul baptized few so no one would follow his name.
unused_candidates.notes: Contains Mormon/Muslim contrasts nearby (18:01–19:55) — avoid those.

unused_candidates.working_title: Can new and mature believers eat at the same table?
unused_candidates.core_truth: Like a family dinner with milk and meat, new and mature believers can be fed in one meeting.
